questions.stem: Fossils are most commonly found in

options.text: sedimentary rock
living cytoplasm
the atmosphere
pure molten magma

questions.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms as layers of mud, sand or lime bury remains. Minerals replace tissues and the impression is kept. Igneous rock crystallises from magma that would destroy organic remains, so fossils are not found there.

distractorRationale.b: Living cytoplasm is not a fossil; a fossil is preserved dead material
distractorRationale.c: The atmosphere does not preserve bones or shells
distractorRationale.d: Molten magma would burn organic remains rather than preserve them

questions.stem: The pentadactyl limb of a human, a bat and a whale is an example of

options.text: analogous structures
homologous structures
vestigial structures only
acquired characters

questions.explanation: The same one-two-many-five bone plan is present even though the limbs now walk, fly or swim. That shared plan from a common ancestor is homology. Analogy would be similar function with different structure, as in an insect wing versus a bird wing.

distractorRationale.a: Analogous organs have the same job but different structure
distractorRationale.c: These limbs are fully functional, not vestigial
distractorRationale.d: Acquired characters are Lamarck's idea, not a class of anatomical evidence

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: The wing of a bird and the wing of a locust are described as analogous because they

options.text: have the same bone arrangement inherited from a flying ancestor
perform the same function but have different underlying structures
are vestigial in both animals
prove that insects descended from birds

questions.explanation: Both wings are used for flight, but a bird wing is a modified pentadactyl limb of bone and feathers while an insect wing is a chitinous outgrowth with no bones. Similar function plus different structure is the definition of analogy and of convergent evolution.

distractorRationale.a: Insects do not have a pentadactyl bone plan; that statement would describe homology
distractorRationale.c: Both wings are functional, not vestigial
distractorRationale.d: Analogy does not mean one group descended from the other

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: Darwin's finches are a classic example of adaptive radiation because

options.text: one ancestral species gave rise to several species with different beaks fitted to different diets
all the finches have identical beaks
the birds acquired longer beaks by stretching them and passed that on
finches have vestigial wings and cannot fly

questions.explanation: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into several niches. On the Galápagos, descendants of one finch stock evolved crushing, probing or picking beaks matching seeds, insects or cactus. The same pattern is seen in West African cichlid fishes.

distractorRationale.b: Identical beaks would show no radiation into different niches
distractorRationale.c: That is Lamarck's rejected mechanism, not adaptive radiation
distractorRationale.d: Darwin's finches fly well; vestigial wings are not part of this example

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: The human appendix and the pelvic bones of a whale are both

options.text: analogous organs used for swimming
vestigial structures reduced from a more functional ancestral form
organs acquired by use during an individual's life
evidence that whales descended from humans

questions.explanation: Vestigial organs are homologous remnants that no longer do the original job: the appendix is a reduced caecum, and whale pelvic bones are leftovers of hind limbs from a land-living ancestor. They support evolution because a designer would not be expected to leave useless copies of ancestral parts.

distractorRationale.a: Neither structure is an analogous swimming organ
distractorRationale.c: They are inherited remnants, not characters acquired in one lifetime
distractorRationale.d: Shared vestiges indicate common ancestry much further back, not that whales came from humans

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: In an undisturbed cliff, fossils in the lowest layers are generally

options.text: younger than those near the top
older than those near the top
exactly the same age as living species
impossible to compare with those above them

questions.explanation: Sediment is laid down on top of older beds, so relative dating reads time from the bottom up. Radioisotopes can then give a numerical age, but the superposition principle already ranks the fossils. That time sequence is a core part of the fossil evidence for evolution.

distractorRationale.a: Younger fossils are in higher, more recently deposited layers
distractorRationale.c: Deep fossils pre-date living species, often by millions of years
distractorRationale.d: Position in the sequence is precisely how they are compared

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: Cichlid fishes in West African crater lakes have diversified into algae-grazers, insect-pickers and predators from shared ancestors. This is evidence of

options.text: adaptive radiation into different niches
the inheritance of acquired feeding habits in Lamarck's sense
analogous structures becoming homologous
a pyramid of energy inverting

questions.explanation: One ancestral stock splitting into several species, each using a different food niche, is adaptive radiation — the same process as Darwin's finches, illustrated with a West African fauna. Feeding habits are not acquired by stretching jaws and then inherited in Lamarck's way.

distractorRationale.b: Radiation is Darwinian diversification, not inheritance of acquired characters
distractorRationale.c: Homology and analogy are anatomical terms; they do not convert into each other here
distractorRationale.d: Energy pyramids belong to ecology, not to this evidence

sources.title: WAEC Biology Syllabus — Evidence for Evolution

questions.stem: Which combination correctly pairs a line of evidence with what it shows?

options.text: Fossil sequence — life has changed through geological time; homologous pentadactyl limbs — common ancestry; insect and bird wings — analogous convergence
Fossil sequence — all species appeared at once; analogous wings — common ancestry; whale pelvis — a structure acquired by swimming
Embryology — insects and birds share a pentadactyl limb; vestigial appendix — analogous to a bat wing
Biochemistry — Lamarckian use and disuse; fossils — adaptive radiation of finch beaks only

questions.explanation: These three lines agree: rocks show change through time, homology shows divergence from a shared plan, and insect versus bird wings show convergence. The other combinations mix up homology with analogy, treat vestiges as acquired characters, or attach biochemistry to Lamarck.

distractorRationale.b: Fossils do not show simultaneous origin; analogous wings are not homology; a whale pelvis is vestigial, not acquired by swimming
distractorRationale.c: Pentadactyl limbs are a vertebrate homology; the appendix is vestigial, not analogous to a wing
distractorRationale.d: Molecular similarity supports common ancestry, not Lamarck; fossils are broader than one finch example

questions.stem: The fossil record provides evidence for evolution primarily by showing that

options.text: species have remained unchanged over time
some species have gone extinct while others have emerged
all species are related to each other
fossils are identical to modern organisms

questions.explanation: The fossil record demonstrates that life on Earth has changed over time, with some species going extinct and new species emerging. This change supports the concept of evolution, indicating that species adapt and evolve in response to environmental changes.

distractorRationale.a: This option is incorrect as it contradicts the evidence provided by fossils showing change over time.
distractorRationale.c: While some species are related, this option oversimplifies the complexity of evolutionary relationships.
distractorRationale.d: Fossils often show differences from modern organisms, indicating evolutionary changes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a vestigial structure?

options.text: The wings of an ostrich
The gills of a fish
The human tailbone

questions.explanation: The human tailbone, or coccyx, is considered a vestigial structure as it is a remnant of a tail that was present in ancestral species. It no longer serves the function of a tail but indicates evolutionary history.

distractorRationale.a: Ostrich wings are not vestigial as they serve the purpose of balance and display.
distractorRationale.b: Gills in fish are functional structures necessary for respiration.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes homologous structures?

options.text: Structures that serve similar functions but have different evolutionary origins
Structures that have the same evolutionary origin but serve different functions
Structures that are present in all organisms
Structures that have no function in the organism

questions.explanation: Homologous structures are those that share a common evolutionary origin but may serve different functions in different species. This reflects how diverse forms can evolve from a common ancestor.

distractorRationale.a: This describes analogous structures, not homologous ones.
distractorRationale.c: Not all organisms share the same structures; this is inaccurate.
distractorRationale.d: This describes vestigial structures, which is not the definition of homologous structures.

questions.stem: Adaptive radiation occurs when

a single ancestor species rapidly diversifies into a variety of forms
species remain unchanged over time
species migrate to new environments

distractorRationale.c: This contradicts the concept of adaptive radiation, which involves change.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures is an example of an analogous structure?

questions.stem: Which of the following best illustrates the concept of convergent evolution?

options.text: The similarity between the limb structures of mammals
The development of similar traits in unrelated species
The evolutionary changes in a single species over time

questions.explanation: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated species develop similar traits due to adaptation to similar environments or ecological niches. This illustrates how similar environmental pressures can lead to similar adaptations.

distractorRationale.a: This describes homologous evolution, not convergent evolution.
distractorRationale.c: This focuses on changes within a species rather than between unrelated species.
distractorRationale.d: This refers to adaptive radiation, which is different from convergent evolution.
